transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you, too. Um, I'm here because... well, I guess some people have been noticing some things about me lately, and I just wanted to make sure everything is okay, if that makes sense? 

It's a little embarrassing, but, um, sometimes it's like I'm moving like I'm underwater. Like, it takes me forever just to answer a question or even get out of a chair. I try not to do it at work, but I guess it happens. And then other times, it's the exact opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands together... almost like I'm trying to shake off a really bad customer service call, you know? It's probably nothing major, but I figured it was best to check in. Am I explaining that right?
During those times when you are pacing and feel restless, do you find that your mind is racing or that you suddenly need much less sleep than usual?

No, no, nothing like that. My mind doesn't race... I mean, I might just be thinking about my grocery list or, you know, what I need to do the next day. It's just normal stuff. And I definitely don't need less sleep. If anything, I try to get my full eight hours. I'm just a little fidgety sometimes, that's all. That's pretty normal, right? Just a little nervous energy?
Have you ever felt this way, with the slow movements or the restlessness, at any other time in your life before these recent months?

Well, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it's actually been going on for a bit longer than just a few months. I hope it's okay I didn't say that right off the bat, I just... I didn't want to make a bigger deal out of it than it is. 

But if I really think about it, it's been happening for, um, maybe about two years and three months? Give or take a little? It started right after I... well, after I was fired from my old customer-support job. It's a little embarrassing to admit that part, losing the job, I mean. I try to just stay positive and move forward. But yeah, that's when the pacing and the slow moments kind of really began. 

Is that helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Over these past two years, have you felt consistently sad, down, or uninterested in things you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't say I'm always completely down, because I really do try to keep a smile on my face, especially around other people. I don't want to be a downer, you know? 

But, if I'm being totally honest... yeah, since I lost that job, there's been this sort of... background feeling of just being sad. And feeling really guilty about losing the job, too. It's like, most of the time, I just don't have the energy or interest to do the things I used to like doing. And my sleep has been kind of messed up, too. 

Some weeks are definitely better than others, and I try really hard to focus on the good days. I just don't want you to think I'm complaining or not trying to get better. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
